recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. Revisit only if the work group opens a new issue to further clarify differential shorthand versus explicit snapshot slicing; that broader tooling question is outside this seed's already-applied source clarification.
issue_request: FHIR-12259 asked FHIR-core to clarify that choice elements remain represented by their original [x] element, type-list restrictions must be applied to that original element, type-specific constraints apply only to that type slice, and ids treat type-specific constraints as slices rather than using @type as the discriminator path.
initial_application: Commit c7c93dc81ec97baf811ceabb97ab0e5ba80b90a2 explicitly applied #12259 by removing the old @type discriminator sentence and adding the current choice-type constraint rules to source/elementdefinition.html. FHIR-16312 later added the complementary ElementDefinition.id type-slice note.
additional_context: FHIR-39180 and FHIR-39182 later changed examples from obsolete choice type renamed paths like Patient.deceasedBoolean to the current full slice form Patient.deceased[x]:deceasedBoolean. Zulip discussion identifies FHIR-12259 as the policy source and supports the later move to full slice syntax. No relevant Confluence evidence was found.
reconciliation: Published an empty audit commit. The current build-source text already states the FHIR-12259 behavior in source/elementdefinition.html and the relevant pages are build-scope inputs, so a source edit would be redundant and risks undoing later approved wording.
